caption: A dropper elevator 4 blocks up (11 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt) fires the column: its observer at the second dropper is placed last (a player starts the clock by placing it), so its partner leads by 2 gt; a chain of observers facing down climbs from the partner a block every 2 gt, and an observer every two blocks fires the next three droppers 4 gt after the ones below (a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it). A dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off.

A dropper elevator 5 blocks up (14 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt) fires the column: its observer at the second dropper fires droppers 0-2 and leads (its partner is placed last: a player starts the clock by placing it); a four-observer bend from it fires droppers 3-5 4 gt later; then a chain of observers facing down climbs a block every 2 gt and an observer every two blocks fires the next three droppers 4 gt after the ones below (a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it). A dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off.

A bubble-column elevator 4 blocks up (40 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a dropper that shoots each item into a water column over soul sand; the bubble column lifts it to the top source, under a ceiling, whose flow toward the flowing water beside it carries it back over the collecting hopper, on the dropper's side (the items drift away from the dropper as they rise, and the hollow under a hopper's rim beside the column would catch one), which pushes it into the output chest. Two observers facing each other in the column's wall are the clock (6 gt): the lower one's back powers the stone above the dropper hard (a hard-powered dropper would lock the hopper beside it); the upper one is placed last (a player starts the clock by placing it). No redstone part grows with the height: the bill stays 10 iron, 2 quartz, 5 redstone (from 4 blocks up: lower, the upper observer's back would lock the collecting hopper).

A bubble-column elevator 3 blocks up (40 blocks) that rests when no item comes: the hopper under the input chest feeds a dropper that shoots each item into a water column over soul sand; the bubble column lifts it to the top source, under a ceiling, whose flow carries it back over the collecting hopper on the dropper's side (the items drift away from the dropper as they rise), which pushes it into the output chest. The dropper's clock runs only while the dropper holds an item: a comparator reads the dropper, and its signal reaches the sticky piston below the cell in front of it (a piston is also powered through the cell above it), which pushes an observer up beside the clock's other observer; the pair then pulses every 6 gt, and the lower one's back powers the stone above the dropper hard (the hopper beside the dropper stays unpowered). With the dropper empty the piston pulls the observer back down and the clock stops.
